title: Skip or Attempt Decision Framework
tagline: Year 4 — A five-question checklist for deciding in ten seconds whether to attempt, eliminate-and-guess, or skip

introduction.overview: The decision to attempt or skip should be quick and rule-based. A five-question checklist works: (1) Do I recognise the type? (2) Is the estimated time within twice my pace? (3) Is my chance of being right above the break-even chance? (4) Can I eliminate options? (5) Is there a quicker question waiting? Each "no" pushes towards skipping; two or more "no" answers mean skip or guess by elimination. The rules and figures used in examples are hypothetical teaching rules, not the policy of any real company or platform.
introduction.placementRelevance: Disciplined skipping is the main difference between candidates of similar ability.
introduction.realWorldContext: Saying no to low-value tasks is a time-management skill.

learningObjectives: Compute break-even and compare with your chance
Decide between attempt, eliminate-and-guess and skip

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Break-even chance = penalty ÷ (marks + penalty). Skip threshold = twice your average pace.

coreDefinitions: Checklist: a fixed list of questions asked of each question.
Skip: leave it (and return if allowed).
Break-even chance: the minimum worthwhile chance.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A fixed checklist removes emotion from the decision.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Ask the five questions in ten seconds; count the "no" answers.

mainNarrative: A question you recognise, estimated at 100 seconds with a 75-second pace (threshold 150 s), with a 70% chance and penalty 0.25: attempt.
A question you do not recognise, estimated at 200 seconds, with chance 25% and elimination possible for two options: two or more "no" answers, so eliminate and guess or skip.
With break-even 20% and chance 15%, skip unless you can eliminate options to lift the chance.
Under no return, convert "skip" into "eliminate and answer" if there is no penalty.
After each mock, count questions you skipped that you could have solved, and tune.

deepDiveAspects.title: Overconfidence
deepDiveAspects.content: Check your actual accuracy on similar questions to calibrate p.

deepDiveAspects.title: Anxiety skips
deepDiveAspects.content: Skipping because a question looks long, not because it is, loses easy marks; apply the checklist.

solvedExamples.title: Time test
solvedExamples.question: Pace 75 s, estimate 100 s. Within the twice-pace threshold?

solvedExamples.title: Break-even
solvedExamples.question: Marks 1, penalty 0.25. Your chance is 15%. Attempt blindly?

solvedExamples.title: Decision
solvedExamples.question: Two "no" answers in the checklist. What do you do?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Ask: recognise? time? chance? eliminate? quicker one waiting? Two or more "no" means skip or guess.

placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Practise the checklist on mock questions.

sourcesAndReferences.sourceName: Official instructions published by each test provider and employer
sourcesAndReferences.referenceNote: Exam patterns and rules change; this chapter teaches how to read and plan around the official instructions and quotes no company-specific figures.
